overall: The AG found the Housing Authority board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in convening an executive session on a complaint against a member, and noted in a footnote, without finding a violation, that the open session minutes were too thin.

allegations.summary: A board member, the subject of a complaint discussion, alleged the board denied his request to have counsel present during the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: While the law affords the subject of a Purpose 1 executive session the right to have counsel present, the law does not require that a public body delay discussion if counsel is not retained.

allegations.summary: A board member alleged the board denied his request to hold the discussion of complaints against him in open session rather than executive session.
allegations.key_passage: It is not a violation of the Open Meeting Law for a public body to express a preference for a discussion to take place in executive session, provided that the body ultimately honors the subject's preferences.

allegations.summary: Although not clearly alleged, the meeting was moved one day later; the AG considered whether the change required new notice.
A board member alleged it was improper for a uniformed police officer to be present during the open and executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: We note that the Open Meeting Law does not prohibit the presence of law enforcement, either during an open session or an executive session.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by the complainant; the AG noted the open session minutes for the meeting were too brief given the roughly 45-minute discussion on the audio.
allegations.key_passage: the minutes of the January 22 open session meeting are insufficiently detailed.
